title: From Equations to PyTorch: Attention and the Transformer Block
summary: Turn the attention and transformer-block equations from the earlier lessons into working PyTorch: positional encodings, a single head, batched multi-head attention, the feed-forward network and a pre-norm block. Shapes are tracked on every line, and the lesson ends with the tests that prove the block is wired correctly.
objectives: Read and predict tensor shapes in the (B, n, d) convention, including nn.Linear and batched matrix multiplies
Implement learned and sinusoidal positional encodings and compute sinusoidal values by hand
Write a causal attention head and a multi-head attention layer using view, transpose and masked_fill, and explain the bugs each line can hide
Implement the GELU feed-forward network and count the parameters of attention, FFN and a whole block
Assemble a pre-norm transformer block and test it for shape, parameter count and causality
prerequisites: You should know the theory from [Attention](/learn/model-foundations/attention) (queries, keys, values, the causal mask, multi-head attention) and [The Transformer Block](/learn/model-foundations/transformer-block) (residual stream, LayerNorm, FFN, positional information). Basic Python is assumed; PyTorch is introduced as needed, starting from tensor shapes.
